trust_decision.summary: Translation msgids/keys from untrusted PO or i18next JSON must never be used as object-path segments, so __proto__/constructor/prototype segments are rejected at every level of key.split(separator) and for bare keys, decided in lib/js2i18next.js and mirrored in the committed browser bundle gettext.js.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names js2i18next(), and this key.split(separator) loop is the first place an untrusted translation key becomes an object path (appendTo[keys[x]] then Object.assign(appendTo, newValues)).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: gettext.js/gettext.min.js are generated browserify+uglify outputs ('not source'), so a solver can claim they are regenerated by npm run build and never edit them, even though the published fix edited both.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate keys containing the keyseparator must still be split into nested objects (and keys that merely contain an unsafe word as a substring must survive), so a fix must match whole segments exactly instead of dropping every separator-bearing key or using substring matching.

O6_input_shapes: keys containing the keyseparator, split into several segments ('__proto__##gcPolluted', 'a##constructor##gcPolluted', 'constructor##prototype##gcPolluted')
bare unsafe keys with no separator ('__proto__', 'constructor', 'prototype')
plural/context-suffixed keys and a custom keyseparator, because the guard runs on segments before suffixing

O7_producer.where: lib/flatten.js:105-203 builds the flat key map consumed by i18next2js/i18next2po; its plural merge at lib/flatten.js:215-233 then indexes flat with the produced key

O8_uncovered_routes.route: i18next2js()/i18next2po() with an i18next key whose base is __proto__ plus a plural suffix (e.g. '__proto___2', '__proto___other'): flatten's plural post-pass reads flat['__proto__'] (Object.prototype) and writes its `plurals` array onto it.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: flatten is the reverse i18next->gettext direction, a separate utility from js2i18next, and the flat map looks internal rather than an object path a caller controls.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 2 files / same package: lib/i18next2js.js:163 -> lib/flatten.js, reached from public i18next2js and i18next2po (lib/i18next2po.js:7)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The same flatten plural merge is present in the committed browser bundle, so loading gettext.js still writes `plurals` onto Object.prototype.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It lives inside a generated bundle, so a solver treats it as out of scope for a library-source fix and relies on a rebuild that would not fix flatten anyway.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: separate module copy in the root bundle file, not reached through lib/

O8b_injection_room.sibling: `trans[kv.context][kv.key] = {...}` builds the js translation table from i18next keys with the same dynamic-key mechanism (also lib/i18next2js.js:137).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer adding an UNSAFE_KEYS guard to the gettext->i18next direction would plausibly mirror it in the reverse converter, since its input file is equally untrusted.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: PO header map writes result[HEADERS.get(lowerKey)] / result[key] from caller-supplied header names.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Header names come from the same PO input; a broad 'sanitize every key taken from input' fix would naturally extend here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: keyasareference writes `data[ctx][id] = x` with an id taken from the PO reference comment.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same function and same loop family; a reviewer asking 'any other dynamic key here' would find it, and a sibling advisory would cover it.

O9_family: prototype pollution (CWE-1321) via translation keys used as object-path segments in a gettext/i18next converter

O10_build.language: JavaScript (Node.js, ESM; Babel-compiled cjs/ and esm/)
O10_build.toolchain: Node.js + npm; Babel 7.28 preset-env; browserify 17 + uglify-js for gettext.js/gettext.min.js; mocha 11 + expect.js
O10_build.project_tests: mocha suite test/test.js: js2i18next at :20-23 and po2i18next at :24-29 against test/fixtures/example-i18next.json; nested-array tests at :110-129; no prototype-pollution tests at the pinned commit. Test imports require ../cjs/<name> (test/test.js:5-6), so npm test builds first (package.json:104).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add `if (key === '__proto__') return` (or a substring/indexOf check) inside lib/js2i18next.js only, rebuild, and validate through js2i18next() alone.

out_of_scope_notes: None — nothing outside this advisory's prototype-pollution protection was noticed or pursued.
